page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c8g1.2xlarge is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8163 processor with 8 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 31.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 3.88 GB per core. Acceleration is delivered via a single bundled NVIDIA T4 GPU based on the Turing architecture, featuring 16 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is not included, and the instance relies on network-attached storage, supported by a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark data highlights a clear contrast between CPU-bound tasks and GPU-accelerated workloads. The Intel Xeon 8163 CPU registers weak performance in single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests, placing in the bottom 25 percent. Similarly, standard database operations, Redis SET performance, and static web serving throughput fall into the bottom 25 percent. However, the integrated NVIDIA T4 GPU delivers strong performance for machine learning tasks. LLM inference speed for prompt processing reaches top-tier status, placing in the top 10 percent, with 8,407.18 tokens per second on a small 135M model and 1,134.43 tokens per second on a medium 7B model. Text generation on the 7B model is also strong, achieving 33.96 tokens per second.

The primary tradeoff of this instance is its reliance on older CPU and GPU architectures, which limits its efficiency for general-purpose compute or high-throughput web serving. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.gn6i-c8g1.2xlarge serves as an entry-level GPU instance, offering a cost-effective entry point for GPU-accelerated workloads without the premium associated with newer-generation accelerators. It is best suited for light AI inference, small-to-medium LLM prompt processing, and basic machine learning model evaluation rather than heavy general-purpose computing or high-IOPS database hosting.
